A1.justification: Both PDFs describe TS-Reasoner and contain readable main texts, figures, tables, equations and appendices. Retained material can be matched across the substantial reorganization.

before.justification: V4 reports original TimeSeriesExam and multi-step inference evaluations, component ablations, generalization experiments and backbone comparisons.

after.justification: V5 retains original empirical results and adds operator ablations, baseline comparisons, and PTF and TSQA evaluations.

M1.justification: The described handling of repeated plans changes: v4 Section 3.3 explicitly prompts reflection and selection of the best buffered solution, whereas v5 Section 3 says execution proceeds directly to completion. This is a limited procedural revision; the decomposer, four operator categories and supplied agent prompt otherwise remain substantively the same.

E1.justification: V5 Appendix A adds two external evaluation datasets: PTF for context-guided forecasting and TSQA for questions about trend, volatility, seasonality and outliers. These substantially broaden evaluation beyond the retained TimeSeriesExam, electricity, weather, synthetic causal and stock-volatility settings. V4's illustrative search-frequency forecasting example is removed.

E2.justification: V5 adds ChatTime, Chronos, ARIMA and AutoGluon to constrained forecasting comparisons, MATMCD and Granger causality to causal discovery, and Z-score to anomaly detection. New appendix benchmarks introduce further forecasting and LLM comparators. V4 Figure 1's illustrative ChatGPT o4-mini-high/4o comparison is removed.

E3.justification: New protocols evaluate PTF with histories of 48–120 steps and a 24-step horizon using MAE, and TSQA at lengths 64–512 using accuracy. Benchmark size is reported as approximately 500 instances instead of 390; v5's cost analysis assumes five interaction turns, versus v4's stated six-turn experimental maximum. Instance-count reconciliation and rerunning of retained results are not established.

E4.justification: V5 Table 3 separately removes custom and retrieval operators, testing their contributions to constraint satisfaction and forecast quality. Removing custom operators reduces reported success from 92.5% to 65%; removing retrieval raises MAPE from 0.1031 to 0.1503. Appendices A–B add sequence-length sensitivity discussion and inference-cost analysis, while earlier feedback and backbone ablations remain.

E5.justification: V5 explicitly discloses a single run for all experiments; v4 specifies deterministic decoding settings without stating the run count. Standard deviations across successful instances remain, with no new confidence intervals, significance tests or repeated-run uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Retained forecasting and backbone values are unchanged, and generalization-table differences are rounding. V5 adds extensive results, including TS-Reasoner's PTF MAE of 0.3672 and TSQA accuracy of 0.9210. New comparisons also reveal exceptions to superiority: ARIMA achieves 0.9625 success without covariates versus TS-Reasoner's 0.9250. These are added findings, not version-to-version performance gains. V4's search-frequency example is removed.

T1.justification: V5's equations and prose recast the existing decomposition, execution and feedback framework. The schematic operator formulas are condensed, but no substantive theoretical result, formal assumption or proof is added or removed.

C1.justification: The agent, multi-step inference paradigm, benchmark and main performance contributions persist. V5 drops v4's universal-task framing and explicitly qualifies causal relationships as Granger-style predictive dependencies in the introduction, modestly narrowing the claimed scope.

C2.justification: V5 explicitly frames the system as decision support, identifies dependence on manually annotated examples and additional toolbox engineering, and qualifies causal interpretation. Diagnostic performance is now discussed as a success–quality tradeoff rather than uniform dominance. New ablations support separate interpretations of custom operators for constraint handling and retrieval for forecast accuracy.

D1.justification: V5 newly documents the 10% temporal pseudo-holdout for intermediate feedback, a 57-operator toolkit count, baseline interpreter/libraries and token-cost accounting. It supplies a named code-and-dataset release link instead of v4's promised release and anonymous samples. Conversely, v4 Appendix H's detailed synthetic causal-data generation prompt is removed, reducing locally documented reproducibility.

R1.justification: V5 adds discussion of context/event-aware forecasting agents and positions TS-Reasoner within the Agent-as-Data-Analyst paradigm. New references include TimeCAP, ChatTime, MATMCD and AutoGluon; Informer and the domain-specialization survey are removed. The central positioning around domain tools and compositional inference remains.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, method exposition and discussion are extensively rewritten. Dataset construction and task templates move from appendices into a dedicated main Section 4; generalization becomes Section 6, limitations are recast, and appendices are reorganized.

P2.justification: V5 adopts a journal layout, relocates the architecture and dataset displays, adds dataset-generation and end-to-end example figures, and expands the result tables. Error-distribution and component-ablation pie charts become stacked bars. The original search-frequency plot is removed, while several other diagrams are reused unchanged.

improvement.justification: Broader specialist, statistical and AutoML comparisons, targeted ablations and external benchmarks strengthen empirical scrutiny. Feedback and limitation disclosures improve transparency. These gains are limited by removal of the causal-generation prompt, blank AutoGluon cells and retained superiority claims despite Table 2 counterexamples. The new cost analysis also reports $0.49 for cached inputs although its displayed formula gives approximately $0.046.
